title: Applied-Energistics-2 issue #8754: Unexpected item consume when enable the replace mode of crafting partterns

text:
[issue by L2750558108]
### Describe the bug

For two crafting recipes, A and B, where A accepts item types T1 and T2, and recipe B only accepts T2. In a crafting tree where recipes A and B need to be crafted in sequence, the material T2 for recipe B is already prepared before crafting recipe A for some reason (possibly due to leftover materials from preparing other recipes). If the replace material option in recipe A's parttern is enabled, when crafting recipe A, the crafting system may prematurely consume the T2 material that was originally intended for recipe B. By the time you get to craft recipe B, only the T1 material that should have been consumed by recipe A remains, making it impossible to craft recipe B, which causes the craft line to get stuck in the planned craft state.

Specifically, when crafting a 256M quantum crafting storage, there are two recipes in sequence: first craft a 1k item storage compent and then a Fluix crystal (used for 2^3 space components). The recipe for the 1k item storage component accepts both regular and charged certus crystals, while the Fluix crystal only accepts charged ones. When crafting the 1k item storage component, it is possible to accidentally use up the charged certus crystals that were intended for the Fluix crystal(because the not charged certus crytus orginally prepare for the recipe is provided by a ME Level Emitter in the certus crytus farm and need time to get), leading to a craft blockage.

### How to reproduce the bug

1. Prepare a crafting line for 256M quantum crafting storage, the fluix crystals is crafted by Reaction Chamber and the certus crytus is provided by a crytus farm
2. Run the craft for 256M quantum crafting storage and wait for the stuck.

### Expected behavior

It should not be stuck

### Additional details

_No response_

### Which minecraft version are you using?

1.21

### On which mod loaders does it happen?

NeoForge

### Crash log

no crash

[comment by Mithi83 (collaborator)]
I think the problem is that the crafting plan is checked once before the start to determine which amount of what material must be reserved for the crafting job. But during the execution of the crafting plan any recipe for producing an intermediate will be exploited, even if that means that a resource is used that in theory should be reserved for another recipe. To avoid that the crafting plan would have to save the specific recipe used during planning rather than just the intended product/intermediate. Changing that could potentially have very serious side effects, as that code is a very complex and central part of the autocrafting.

I vaguely remember someone (Technici4n?) talk about something like that during the progress bar fix changes.

For your specific problem however I‘d suggest to disable substitution in the 1k storage component and make it regular certus only.

[comment by Mari023 (collaborator)]
Implementing #5597 would likely fix this.

[comment by Mithi83 (collaborator)]
That is exactly what I was looking for :)

[comment by L2750558108 (none)]
Checking these kinds of synthesis problems is really awful, especially on those long synthesis chains. This time, it took me nearly three days to figure out what happened.

It seems that if I want to completely avoid this problem before the fix pull request, I can't enable replacement mode on any template, because once it's enabled, there could be potential risks. But not using replacement mode at all would mean that I might need to write a different template for every type of board. I think that's not really reasonable. Is there any other thing I can do before the fix commit?

[comment by Mithi83 (collaborator)]
I would not go as far as to generally disable substitution. Substitution mode is still useful for other situations, e.g. to ignore durability in the cutting knifes for facades. As a heuristic in the AE2 area you could disable substitution for all recipes that allow certus quartz or charged certus quartz as an alternative.

If by „every type of board“ you mean the different types of wood, then maybe you don‘t want to use all types of wood to mass-craft chests if you only keep limited amounts of more rare types in stock for decorative purposes and have one farm that mass-produces oak logs for your regular crafting needs.

[comment by Mari023 (collaborator)]
It is only really problematic if you need a specific variant for some recipes, and any variant for others.
If you are only crafting chests, sticks and crafting tables, the exact wood types usually don't matter, and you can keep substitutions on.

Imo it is a bad idea in general to enable substitutions on items that aren't directly equivalent (charged certus is strictly more expensive than non-charged)

Tho I agree it is quite annoying in general.
